source: AOPK CR (Agentura ochrany prirody a krajiny Ceske republiky / Nature Conservation Agency of the Czech Republic), Pamatne stromy (Memorial Trees)
endpoint: https://gis.nature.cz/arcgis/rest/services/PamatneStromy/PamatneStromy/MapServer/1 (layer 1, 'Pamatne stromy - jedinci', esriGeometryPoint, outSR=4326 served natively)
licence_proof: AOPK CR's own metadata for this dataset, verbatim: "Tato datova sada poskytovana Agenturou ochrany prirody a krajiny Ceske republiky podleha licenci Creative Commons Uvedte puvod 4.0 Mezinarodni" (Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International). Layer copyrightText on the MapServer service itself: "(c) AOPK CR". Recorded in OPEN_DATA_SURVEY.md line 230 (2026-07-30 scan) and re-verified live 2026-08-15.
designation: Pamatny strom, designated under Section 46 of Act No. 114/1992 Coll. on Nature and Landscape Protection (Czech Republic's legal category for individually protected trees)
scope: Individually-positioned single trees only (TYP=1, 'jednotlivy strom' in the source's own typology) out of the full PamatneStromy layer, which also carries TYP=2 ('stromoradi', avenues) and TYP=3 ('skupina stromu', groups of trees). Those two types were NOT imported: the source stores one point per MEMBER TREE within a named avenue or group (one avenue, e.g. 'Haugwitzova alej', holds 171 separate point rows sharing one KOD), so importing them as individual entries would misrepresent a single designated ensemble as dozens of unrelated collectible trees. 4,301 of the layer's 16,795 total points are TYP=1. A future pass could aggregate the TYP=2/3 points per KOD into proper ensemble entries (Portugal's register does this with its 'Alameda' and 'Conjunto arboreo' tipo values) if that becomes worth the work; until then they are left unimported rather than misshapen.
caveat: Five things a run must know before using this. (1) girth_cm (source field OBVOD_V) reads correctly in centimetres already, sanity-checked: values range 1cm to 1,650cm (16.5m) with a plausible mean around 390cm, no metres-mislabelled-as-centimetres pattern found. 202 entries carry OBVOD_V=0 in the source (unmeasured, not a zero-girth tree); those are stored here as girth_cm: null, not 0. (2) No age field exists anywhere in this register, matching the standing note that no Czech source carries one (CLAUDE.md, Trieste learning); age must come from another source per tree. (3) No dedicated vitality field exists, but the free-text note_cz field (source POZNAMKA) sometimes carries an explicit death or deregistration signal in Czech ('zanikly strom' = vanished/extinct tree, 'ochrana zrusena' = protection cancelled, plus specific causes like 'v r. 1996 pravdepodobne spadl pri bouri' = probably fell in a storm in 1996, '21.8.1980 spadla pri vichrici' = fell in a windstorm). 24 of the 4,301 entries carry such a signal and are marked publishable: false with the raw Czech sentence preserved in death_signal; NONE of the 24 should ever ship as a live entry without independent re-verification, per the standing dead-tree rule. This is the same class of error the Lazio removed-trees sheet caught in Rome: a register carrying its own quiet death record inside a field nothing else reads. (4) last_changed (ZMENA_T) is a YYYYMMDD integer for when AOPK's own record was last updated, not when the tree was last surveyed alive; most entries show a 2025-07-15 bulk refresh date, which is a data-maintenance date rather age or life evidence. (5) One duplicate KOD found among TYP=1 (103344, 'Dub u Bucku', two OBJECTIDs, same name, PORADI 1 and 2): almost certainly two physically separate trees sharing one designation (a twin pair), not a fetch error; fold-or-keep-separate is a city-pass judgement per the standing twins rule.
